item.title: Manteca takes care of Cougars in boys volleyball season opener
item.description: Manteca opened its boys volleyball season at home Wednesday with a 25-20, 25-15, 25-13 over Weston Ranch.

item.title: Buffs thump Lodi in shutout, improve to 6-0
item.description: Manteca’s Jeremy Cross threw four innings of two-hit ball and Nate Slikker knocked in three runs for the host Buffaloes, going 2 for 3 with a double and stolen base in a 10-0 five-inning mercy-rule shortened thumping of Lodi in non-league baseball action on Wednesday.

item.title: Lancers rally late to spoil River Islands’ comeback
item.description: The East Union boys volleyball team was unrecognizable to its coach on Wednesday when the Lancers hosted River Islands for a non-league match. And that’s a good thing.

item.title: Two wrongs don’t make a right: Two flags, two National Park Service units
item.description: A granite wall in Yosemite and a “Stonewall” in New York City are now flash points in the ongoing cultural wars. Yosemite, because of a transgender banner that was put up, and New York City, because of a Pride flag that was taken down.

item.title: MYF Ambassador program builds next generation of leaders
item.description: For more than three decades, the Manteca Youth Focus (MYF) Scholarship Competition has helped shape young leaders through leadership development, volunteer service, and educational scholarships.

item.title: SJ County resale homes 71% less than Santa Clara
item.description: There was a time a decade or so ago when a housing dollar in the resale market went close to 60 percent farther in San Joaquin County than in Santa Clara County where a growing number of Manteca-Lathrop-Ripon residents commute to jobs.

item.title: Private sector building value tops $595M in Manteca during 2025
item.description: The value of private sector construction Manteca — fueled by two new shopping centers, a 100-unit apartment complex and 840 single family homes — topped $595 million in 2025.

item.title: Speculation about an EU High employee, chatter continues over pickleball
item.description: A flurry of social media postings making all kinds of statements that surfaced Wednesday about an East Union High employee that has been placed on administrative leave prompted the Manteca Unified School District to issue a statement.

item.description: What constitutes “playground talk” when words such as “gun” are uttered?

item.description: Ongoing damage to Lincoln Park on Powers Avenue was perplexing city officials.
